newsitem.title: USA: U.S. envoy to France said to be near death.
newsitem.headline: U.S. envoy to France said to be near death.

text.p: U.S. ambassador to France Pamela Harriman suffered a massive stroke and is near death at a hospital in Paris, CNN reported on Monday, quoting a senior administration official.

The network said Harriman reportedly collapsed at home while exercising earlier on Monday and was rushed to a hospital, where she remained unconscious. The administration official said Harriman was "very close to death."
No comment was immediately available from the State Department.

Harriman, 76, whose full name is Pamela Digby Churchill Hayward Harriman, was born in Farnborough, England, and became a naturalized U.S. citizen after marrying her third husband, the late multimillionaire financier and diplomat W. Averell Harriman in 1971.

Her first marriage was during the Second World War at age 19 to Randolph Churchill, a journalist, hard-drinking rake and son of British leader Winston Churchill, who adored her and whom she fondly called "papa." They were divorced as the war ended.

Harriman was national co-chairman of the 1992 Clinton-Gore presidential campaign. After President Bill Clinton was elected in 1992, one of his first stops in Washington was a dinner party at Harriman's posh Georgetown home. For her favors to his party, Clinton named her ambassador to France in 1993, one of the plushest of diplomatic appointments.
